full_judgment: 22. Fourth-twelfth defendants-opposite-parties though, in 11(e) paragraph of written statement tabled the case that plaintiff is not daughter of Kala Chand Basak rather, she is daughter of Krishna Chandra Basak, did not at all enter their appearance during trial and did not examine themselves nor did produce any witness in support of the said contention contended in 11(e) paragraph of written statement. Evidence provided by plaintiff as PW 1 in respect of her heirship from her father Kala Chand Basak could be endeavoured to be flung to the winds by way of cross-examination from side of fourth-twelfth defendants but plaintiff PW 1 was not at all cross-examined from side of fourth-twelfth defendants. Cross-examination of a witness is the greatest legal engine for discovery of the truth. Cross-examination is directed to bring to light truth by clarifying matters which a witness may deserve to keep concealed. Failure on the part of fourth-twelfth defendants-opposite parties to cross-examine plaintiff PW 1 definitely raises presumption and legal inference that evidence provided by plaintiff PW 1 in examination-in-chief has been accepted by fourth-twelfth defendants. Support for the proposition of law is sought to be drawn from authoritative observation of  Lord Chancellor Herschell in the case of Browne vs Dunn (1983)6, R 67, AEG Carapiet vs AY Derderain, 1961 Calcutta 359 DB and Nur Mohammad and another vs Sultan Ahmed and another, 40 DLR 369.
